title.narrative: United Nations Joint Programme on HIV/AIDS (UNAIDS) Core Contributions 2022-23 to 2026-27

description.narrative: Core funding contributions to the Joint UN Programme on HIV/AIDS (UNAIDS) for financial years 2022-23 to 2026-27, and totalling $25 million. This investment assists with collecting data and reporting on the epidemic, drafting national HIV plans, amending discriminatory legislation and policies, expanding access to HIV services, applying for and implementing HIV funding from external sources. UNAIDS' engagement with civil society and key affected populations is critical for leveraging maximum impact from Australia's other investments in global health, including our investment in the Global Fund to Fight AIDS, TB and Malaria. The investment is guided by Australia's Strategic Partnership Framework with UNAIDS 2022-27, which focusses on improving HIV outcomes in the Indo-Pacific and strengthening UNAIDS' effectiveness and impact.

title.narrative: United Nations Joint Programme on HIV/AIDS (UNAIDS) Core Contributions 2022-23 to 2026-27

description.narrative: Australia's core contribution to UNAIDS for the period 2023-28 is AUD25 million. UNAIDS assists countries to strengthen their national HIV responses. In 2022-23, in response to mounting humanitarian crisis, the Joint Programme intensified coordination efforts to ensure the continuation of lifesaving HIV services in humanitarian settings, including the delivery of HIV prevention and diagnostics in Ukraine. More broadly, the Joint Programme disseminated updated maternal and new-born health operational guidelines integrating HIV, as well as an interagency field guide for TB prevention and care among refugees and other populations in humanitarian settings, and training and learning packages to support LGBTQ+ people in displacement. At the December 2023 Global Refugee Forum, the Joint Programme advocated for refugee inclusion in national health systems through multisectoral actions where 49 countries pledged to support health, mental health and psychosocial support and health systems strengthening, including for HIV prevention, treatment and services.

Australia’s contributions to UNAIDS in strengthening HIV responses
UNAIDS remains a critical technical partner for the HIV response in our region. It provides technical support for Global Fund-financed HIV programs, which sustained HIV treatment for 3 million people in the Indo-Pacific in 2023. The collective efforts of countries, UNAIDS, and development partners have resulted in a 14% reduction in new HIV infections in the region since 2010, and a 51% reduction in HIV-related deaths. UNAIDS support has been critical in key areas of the HIV response in our region including: increasing treatment and prevention service coverage for key populations, with increased access to highly effective pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP) drugs; sensitizing adolescents and young people on HIV prevention; increasing access to HIV self-testing; and, reducing stigma, discrimination and human rights violations against key populations.
Results reflect a broad definition of “Indo-Pacific” and include Afghanistan, Bangladesh, Bhutan, Cambodia, Cook Islands, Fiji, India, Indonesia, Kiribati, Laos, Marshall Islands, Micronesia, Mongolia, Myanmar, Nauru, Nepal, Niue, Pakistan, Palau, Papua New Guinea, the Philippines, Samoa, Solomon Islands, Sri Lanka, Thailand, Timor-Leste, Tonga, Tuvalu, Vanuatu and Vietnam.

The Joint United Nations Programme on HIV/AIDS continues to lead coordination of global efforts to end AIDS as a public health threat. In 2024, the UNAIDS Secretariat and its co-sponsoring agencies supported 85 countries around the world to strengthen their HIV responses. For example, UNAIDS helped to advance HIV prevention, including enabling expanded access to groundbreaking long-acting HIV prevention technologies. The Joint Program also supported countries to remove punitive and discriminatory laws and policies and expand rights-based HIV programs, helping to reduce stigma and discrimination. To support more financially sustainable HIV programs, UNAIDS provided analysis and guidance, enabling countries and partners such as the Global Fund to Fight AIDS, Tuberculosis and Malaria to make high-impact and efficient investments. ‍ Our region – Asia and the Pacific – is home to some of the fastest growing HIV epidemics in the world. UNAIDS is helping countries track and respond to these epidemics. In 2024, the Joint Program provided technical support across the region, including expanding HIV prevention with PrEP, dapivirine ring, and harm reduction services; boosting HIV testing through self-testing and virtual interventions in over 15 countries; and strengthening regional coordination via new HIV Prevention Task Force and action plans in 11 countries.
